info.title: wpf-locator-doctor: rates how easy a WPF app is to automate, and says exactly what to fix.
info.description: Testability scorecard for WPF apps: checks the AutomationIds your UI tests depend on, scores each screen from 0 to 100, and tells you the exact line of XAML to add. This package contains the source scan, which runs on Windows, macOS and Linux. The live scan of a running app is a separate Windows download on the GitHub releases page.

options.name: --out
options.description: Where to write the reports (default: ./testability-report)

options.name: --baseline
options.description: A previous report; checks that its IDs are still there

options.name: --min-score
options.description: Exit with code 1 if the overall score is lower (for build pipelines)

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Print only where the reports were written

options.name: --source
options.description: Project source, to learn where each ID comes from

options.name: --uia2
options.description: Use the older UIA2 engine (some WPF controls report better with it)

options.name: --wait
options.description: How long to wait for the main window (default 30)

options.name: --max-elements
options.description: Stop after this many elements per window (default 5000)

options.name: --max-rows
options.description: Rows to check per list or grid (default 50)

options.name: --keep-open
options.description: Leave the app running if this tool started it
